exposure: antibiotic treatment during the first year of life
cohort: 1522 preschool children in Urumqi (779 boys and 743 girls), with a control group of children who had never had pneumonia, matched 1:1 based on gender, age, and ethnicity
finding: Several indoor environmental factors, including passive smoking during the mother's pregnancy, certain housing types and flooring materials, and indoor dampness, were associated with an increased risk of pneumonia in preschool children, while the use of fresh air filtration systems was found to be protective.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was associated with an increased risk of pneumonia (OR = 1.27; 95%CI = 1.08–1.48).
